programmes.name: BISP Poverty Scorecard census (NSER) rollout
programmes.agency: Benazir Income Support Programme with RSPN, PCO and survey firms
programmes.window: 2009 test phase (16 districts) then national rollout 2010-2011
programmes.stagger: Phase-in: districts entered the poverty census on different dates because multiple third-party firms worked in parallel
programmes.assign: Administrative sequencing by contracted survey firm and cluster; not random but plausibly unrelated to short-run outcomes
programmes.timing_src: BISP/NSER MIS district census start and completion dates; RSPN and OPM evaluation annexes; ADB and World Bank project documents
programmes.ident: Cleanest large-scale staggered treatment in Pakistan. Use the district census completion date as the event date: eligibility, and hence cash, could only begin once a district was surveyed. OPM's evaluation explicitly notes payments began in some districts before the census had finished in others.
programmes.threats: Firms may have been assigned easier or nearer districts first; 2010 floods interrupted fieldwork in Sindh and south Punjab; concurrent flood cash grants (Watan Card)
programmes.evidence: OPM/Oxford Policy Management BISP impact evaluation series (2011-2016); Cheema et al.; Ambler & De Brauw (2017)

programmes.name: BISP Kafaalat unconditional cash transfer (first payment)
programmes.window: 2008-09 parliamentarian phase; scorecard-based enrolment 2010-2016; continuous expansion since
programmes.stagger: Continuous phase-in of coverage intensity plus discrete district start dates
programmes.assign: PMT score cut-off (16.17, later 32.5 then 37) within districts; district entry follows the census sequence
programmes.timing_src: BISP MIS payment records by district and quarter; BISP annual reports
programmes.ident: Two designs stack neatly: (i) staggered district DiD on the first-payment date, (ii) RD at the PMT cut-off within district. The interaction identifies whether the transfer works differently where coverage is dense.
programmes.threats: General-equilibrium spillovers within districts break SUTVA when coverage is high; inflation eroded the real transfer over time
programmes.evidence: OPM final evaluation (2016); Haseeb & Vyborny (2022) on payment mechanisms

programmes.name: BISP payment-mechanism modernisation (Post -> smart card -> debit card -> biometric)
programmes.agency: BISP with NADRA and partner banks
programmes.window: Pilots in 4-5 districts 2011-12; district-by-district conversion to Benazir Debit Card 2012-2016; biometric verification 2017-2019
programmes.stagger: Sequential district conversion between payment technologies
programmes.assign: Administrative and bank-partner readiness; pilots selected purposively
programmes.timing_src: BISP MIS; OPM process evaluations; SBP branchless banking newsletters
programmes.ident: A rare chance to identify the effect of payment technology holding transfer size fixed. Event study on the conversion date with beneficiary-level MIS data.
programmes.threats: Bank partner assignment correlates with urbanisation and agent density
programmes.evidence: Haseeb & Vyborny (2022) 'Imposing institutions'; OPM process evaluations

programmes.name: BISP Waseela-e-Taleem (primary education CCT)
programmes.window: Launched November 2012 in 5 districts; expanded in waves to ~50 districts by 2016; effectively nationwide by 2020
programmes.stagger: Classic multi-wave district phase-in
programmes.assign: Districts selected on low enrolment and administrative readiness; waves announced by BISP board
programmes.timing_src: BISP annual reports and board minutes; Ehsaas policy documents; World Bank project appraisal documents
programmes.ident: Textbook staggered adoption. Combine ASER district-year learning and enrolment data with the launch date for a Callaway-Sant'Anna event study.
programmes.threats: Concurrent provincial stipend schemes; selection of low-enrolment districts implies mean reversion - check pre-trends carefully
programmes.evidence: Meta-analysis cited in Ehsaas documents finds enrolment gains but weak attendance and learning effects

programmes.name: Ehsaas Taleemi Wazaif (redesigned education CCT)
programmes.window: District-wise digital rollout 2020-2022 replacing Waseela-e-Taleem
programmes.stagger: Phase-in by district as biometric enrolment desks were established
programmes.assign: Administrative rollout schedule
programmes.timing_src: BISP MIS; Ehsaas progress reports
programmes.ident: Difference from P04 is the digitised compliance monitoring. Treat the switch as a separate event and test whether the redesign added value over the paper-based scheme.
programmes.threats: Overlaps with COVID school closures - the confound is severe in 2020-21
programmes.evidence: Limited independent evaluation to date

programmes.name: Ehsaas Nashonuma (nutrition CCT with specialised nutritious food)
programmes.window: Phase 1 in 9 districts (2020), expanded to 13-15 districts (2021), further expansion thereafter
programmes.stagger: Phase-in with a small treated set
programmes.assign: Districts chosen on stunting prevalence in consultation with provincial health departments
programmes.timing_src: Ehsaas and BISP progress reports; WFP country office documents; press releases naming districts
programmes.ident: Small N of treated districts means inference must be done carefully (wild-cluster bootstrap or randomisation inference). Explicit targeting on high stunting demands strong pre-trend evidence.
programmes.threats: Deliberate selection on the outcome (stunting) creates mean reversion; NNS 2018 is the only district-representative anthropometry baseline
programmes.evidence: WFP process evaluations; no published causal evaluation yet

programmes.name: Punjab Zewar-e-Taleem (girls' secondary stipend)
programmes.window: Phased across 16-17 low-literacy districts, 2017-2019
programmes.stagger: Discrete district set, entering in phases
programmes.assign: Selected on low female literacy rate - a deterministic rule on a running variable
programmes.timing_src: PSPA programme documents and district lists; Punjab ADP releases
programmes.ident: Because selection uses a literacy threshold, a fuzzy RD on the district female literacy rate complements the staggered DiD. This is one of the few Pakistani programmes with a near-deterministic assignment rule.
programmes.threats: Targeting on low literacy generates mechanical mean reversion; overlaps with the older Punjab Female School Stipend Programme in several districts
programmes.evidence: Related evidence: Chaudhury & Parajuli (2010) on the earlier Punjab stipend

src.title: Punjab Social Protection Authority — Zewar-e-Taleem Program

programmes.name: Punjab Female School Stipend Programme (PFSSP)
programmes.agency: Punjab Education Department with World Bank
programmes.window: 15 low-literacy districts from 2004; later extension
programmes.stagger: One-shot with a sharp assignment rule, plus later extension waves
programmes.assign: Districts with 1998 census literacy below 40% - a sharp cut-off
programmes.timing_src: World Bank PESRP documents; Chaudhury & Parajuli (2010)
programmes.ident: The canonical Pakistani regression-discontinuity-in-district-characteristics design. Still under-exploited for long-run outcomes (marriage age, fertility, labour supply of the treated cohorts, now in their 30s).
programmes.threats: Only 34 districts existed in 1998 - very few observations near the cut-off; district splits after 2005 complicate the panel
programmes.evidence: Chaudhury & Parajuli (2010, Applied Economics); Alam, Baez & Del Carpio (2011)

programmes.name: Ehsaas Kafaalat expansion and re-survey (NSER 2019-21)
programmes.window: Desk pilot in 4 districts (2016-17); Phase 1 from January 2017; full re-survey 2019-2021
programmes.stagger: Phase-in of the dynamic registry re-survey
programmes.assign: Survey firm cluster assignment
programmes.timing_src: BISP/NSER MIS; ADB Integrated Social Protection Development Program documents
programmes.ident: The re-survey changed who was eligible. Event study on the re-survey date identifies the effect of updating the targeting register (entry and exit of beneficiaries).
programmes.threats: COVID-19 emergency cash coincided with the re-survey window
programmes.evidence: ADB and World Bank supervision reports

programmes.name: Ehsaas Interest-Free Loans (Akhuwat partnership)
programmes.window: District-wise expansion of loan centres 2019-2022
programmes.stagger: Sequential opening of loan centres
programmes.assign: Partner NGO capacity and existing Akhuwat footprint
programmes.timing_src: PPAF and Akhuwat progress reports; Ehsaas dashboards
programmes.ident: Combine centre opening dates with PMN MicroWatch quarterly district penetration to measure crowd-in or crowd-out of commercial microfinance.
programmes.threats: Akhuwat's pre-existing footprint is correlated with district development
programmes.evidence: Limited published evaluation

programmes.name: Punjab Khidmat Card / Himmat Card (disability transfer)
programmes.window: Phased district rollout 2016-2019, relaunched 2024
programmes.stagger: Phase-in
programmes.assign: Administrative capacity and Special Education Department registers
programmes.timing_src: PSPA reports; Punjab ADP
programmes.ident: Useful mainly as a placebo or as an outcome-side treatment for a narrow population.
programmes.threats: Very small treated population; poorly documented dates
programmes.evidence: None known

programmes.name: Ehsaas / BISP Emergency Cash (COVID-19)
programmes.window: April-July 2020 phase 1; 2021 phase 2
programmes.stagger: Compressed staggering over weeks, not years
programmes.assign: Existing NSER register plus SMS-based demand-driven applications
programmes.timing_src: BISP MIS with payment dates; Ehsaas dashboards
programmes.ident: Weekly variation in district payment timing can be exploited with high-frequency outcomes (mobile money, nightlights, mandi prices), but the window is short and overlaps with lockdowns.
programmes.threats: Simultaneous lockdown policy and mobility collapse; payment timing correlates with district population
programmes.evidence: Various rapid assessments; no strong causal study

programmes.name: Prime Minister's National Health Programme / Federal Sehat Sahulat (SSP-I and II)
programmes.agency: Ministry of NHSR&C with State Life Insurance Corporation
programmes.scope: National (federal, Punjab, KP, ICT, AJK, GB)
programmes.window: Launched 31 December 2015 in an initial district set; SSP-II reached 67 districts by 2019
programmes.stagger: Multi-phase district activation
programmes.assign: Districts selected on multidimensional poverty rank and hospital network readiness; eligibility inside districts set by BISP PMT below 32.5
programmes.timing_src: SSP MIS and provincial health department notifications; Sehat Sahulat programme history page; NADRA enrolment records
programmes.ident: The strongest health-finance staggered design in Pakistan. Pair district activation dates with HIES out-of-pocket spending and DHIS/SLIC claims. The within-district PMT cut-off gives a complementary RD.
programmes.threats: Empanelled hospitals are concentrated in cities, so effective access varies within district; supply response (new private hospitals) is itself an outcome
programmes.evidence: Descriptive reviews only (Khan et al. KMUJ 2022; MDPI IJERPH 2022); the causal literature is essentially open

programmes.name: KP Sehat Card Plus (universal provincial coverage)
programmes.window: Four pilot districts from December 2015 (Malakand, Kohat, Mardan, Chitral; poorest ~21% of households); ~24 districts by 2017; all districts and 100% of the population from 20 August 2020
programmes.stagger: Four documented phases with expanding population and benefit coverage
programmes.assign: Pilot districts chosen administratively; later expansion political and universal
programmes.timing_src: KP Health Department notifications; Sehat Card Plus programme history; KMUJ review
programmes.ident: Two treatments in one: extensive margin (district entry) and intensive margin (share of population covered rising from 21% to 100%). A dose-response event study is feasible.
programmes.threats: The 2020 universalisation coincides with COVID; merged districts entered with the FATA merger
programmes.evidence: Lancet Regional Health SEA commentary (2022); KMUJ review; no rigorous causal estimate published

programmes.window: DG Khan and Sahiwal divisions first (2021, ~7 districts); Lahore January 2022; remaining divisions to all 36 districts by March 2022

programmes.timing_src: Punjab Health Department notifications; SSP MIS; press coverage of division launch dates
programmes.ident: Month-level activation dates across 36 districts within one year is exceptionally good variation. Use monthly DHIS admissions, SLIC claims and quarterly HIES modules.

programmes.evidence: No published causal evaluation - a clear gap

programmes.name: Contracting out of Basic Health Units (PRSP / PPHI)
programmes.agency: Provincial governments with Rural Support Programmes (PRSP, SRSO, SRSP, NRSP)
programmes.window: Rahim Yar Khan pilot 2003; expansion to 82-83 districts across four provinces 2005-2013
programmes.stagger: Staggered handover of the district's BHU network to an RSP
programmes.assign: Provincial decisions; documented district-level roll-out dates
programmes.timing_src: Malik, van de Poel & van Doorslaer (2017) assembled the district roll-out dates from PPHI/CMPHI administration; provincial health department notifications
programmes.ident: Already-collected district roll-out dates exist in the published literature - a large fixed cost is already paid. Re-analyse with modern staggered estimators and richer outcomes (DHIS, MICS) than the original paper used.
programmes.threats: Contracting was often reversed or renegotiated (Punjab took BHUs back and re-contracted through PHFMC); treatment is not absorbing
programmes.evidence: Malik, van de Poel & van Doorslaer (2017, Health Policy & Planning); Loevinsohn et al. on Rahim Yar Khan

programmes.name: Punjab Health Facility Management Company outsourcing (second wave)
programmes.window: Low-performing districts first (Nankana Sahib, Bahawalnagar, Narowal, Mandi Bahauddin), then wider expansion 2016-2019
programmes.stagger: Phase-in, with facility-level assignment inside districts
programmes.assign: Explicitly targeted at low-performing districts and facilities
programmes.timing_src: PHFMC annual reports; Punjab Health Department notifications; Dawn coverage of the phased plan
programmes.ident: Facility-level assignment inside districts allows a within-district design that removes district-level political confounds - much stronger than a pure district DiD.
programmes.threats: Selection on low performance guarantees mean reversion; contract terms changed across waves
programmes.evidence: Limited published evaluation

programmes.name: Rescue 1122 emergency service district expansion
programmes.scope: Punjab (then replicated in KP, Sindh, Balochistan, GB, AJK)
programmes.window: Lahore pilot 14 October 2004; phased expansion reaching all 36 Punjab districts by roughly 2010-2015; tehsil-level expansion from 2018
programmes.stagger: Staggered district-by-district launch over roughly a decade
programmes.assign: Sequencing driven by budget releases and political priority; the third-party evaluation of the pilot triggered scale-up
programmes.timing_src: Punjab Emergency Service annual reports and district pages; Punjab P&D ADP scheme documents (district-wise rescue station schemes)
programmes.ident: A rare public-service treatment with a hard, dated switch-on and a mechanically linked outcome (response time, trauma mortality). Also usable as a first stage for the effect of emergency care on road-accident mortality.
programmes.threats: Roads and vehicle fleets expanded simultaneously; crash reporting improves precisely because the service exists (measurement endogeneity)
programmes.evidence: Descriptive Rescue 1122 statistics; almost no causal work

programmes.name: Lady Health Worker Programme coverage expansion
programmes.agency: National Programme for Family Planning & Primary Health Care
programmes.window: Continuous expansion; district coverage intensity varies through the 2000s and 2010s
programmes.stagger: Continuous dose rather than sharp switch-on
programmes.assign: Sanctioned posts by district; recruitment constrained by literate female supply
programmes.timing_src: National Programme MIS; PSLM LHW visit module; third-party evaluations (OPM 2000, 2002, 2009)
programmes.ident: Better treated as a continuous treatment (coverage share) than a binary event. The PSLM LHW module gives a household-reported visit measure that can validate administrative coverage.
programmes.threats: Coverage is placed where female literacy allows recruitment - strongly endogenous to development
programmes.evidence: OPM third-party evaluations; Wazir, Shaikh & Ahmed (2013)

programmes.name: Punjab Aab-e-Pak / Saaf Pani filtration plant programme
programmes.agency: Punjab Saaf Pani Company, later Aab-e-Pak Authority
programmes.window: Phased tenders and installations 2015-2018 (suspended, then relaunched 2019-2022)
programmes.unit: Tehsil / union council, aggregable to district
programmes.treated: Subset of districts, southern Punjab prioritised
programmes.stagger: Phase-in by tender lot
programmes.assign: Arsenic and bacteriological contamination mapping plus political priority
programmes.timing_src: Punjab Saaf Pani Company and Aab-e-Pak Authority plant registers with commissioning dates; Punjab ADP
programmes.ident: Plant-level GPS and commissioning dates allow a distance-based design (households within X km of a plant) rather than a coarse district DiD.
programmes.threats: Programme was suspended amid a corruption inquiry, so treatment is non-absorbing; plant functionality is far below installation counts
programmes.evidence: Audit and NAB reports; no causal evaluation

programmes.name: EPI strengthening, IPV introduction and polio campaign intensification
programmes.agency: EPI / National and Provincial Emergency Operations Centres with WHO and UNICEF
programmes.window: IPV introduced 2015; district risk classification and campaign intensity vary by round from 2014
programmes.unit: District / union council, by campaign round
programmes.stagger: High-frequency continuous variation in campaign rounds rather than a single switch
programmes.assign: Risk classification based on environmental surveillance and case history
programmes.timing_src: EOC campaign records; WHO LQAS reports; DHIS immunisation module
programmes.ident: Very high frequency (campaign rounds every few weeks) supports precise event studies for routine immunisation spillovers.
programmes.threats: Deliberate targeting of high-risk districts; security incidents against vaccinators are correlated with conflict outcomes
programmes.evidence: Large public health literature; little economics

programmes.name: COVID-19 smart lockdowns and vaccination centre rollout
programmes.agency: NCOC with provincial governments and NADRA/NIMS
programmes.window: Smart lockdowns by district and union council, March 2020 onward; vaccination centres phased by district and age band, February 2021 onward
programmes.stagger: Genuine week-by-week district variation in restriction status
programmes.assign: Positivity-rate thresholds set by NCOC - a rule-based running variable
programmes.timing_src: NCOC daily situation reports; NIMS vaccination MIS; provincial notifications
programmes.ident: Positivity thresholds create a fuzzy RD in addition to the staggered DiD. Mobility (Google/Meta), nightlights and mandi prices give weekly outcomes.
programmes.threats: Enormous simultaneity - everything moved at once in 2020; positivity depends on testing, which is itself endogenous
programmes.evidence: Some rapid-response work; the district-level economics is largely unwritten

programmes.name: PEF Foundation Assisted Schools (FAS)
programmes.window: Launched 2005 in 6 districts; ten expansion phases to province-wide coverage
programmes.stagger: Ten documented expansion phases
programmes.assign: Districts added by phase; schools within districts qualify by passing a Quality Assurance Test
programmes.timing_src: PEF phase notifications and partner school registers with partnership dates; PEF annual reports
programmes.ident: Two levels of variation: district phase entry and school-level QAT pass/fail (the QAT score threshold is a genuine RD). Barrera-Osorio & Raju exploited the school-level cut-off; the district phase-in is still open.
programmes.threats: Partner schools are self-selected private schools; displacement of public enrolment is a real outcome, not a nuisance
programmes.evidence: Barrera-Osorio & Raju (2015, 2017) on the FAS QAT discontinuity; ADB (2010) case study

programmes.name: PEF Education Voucher Scheme (EVS)
programmes.window: Fifteen-plus expansion phases; phase 15 alone covered 16 districts (2015); reached 28+ districts
programmes.stagger: Repeated district-level expansion phases with named district lists
programmes.assign: Districts selected on out-of-school population and katchi abadi presence; households qualify on income
programmes.timing_src: PEF phase press releases naming districts and dates; PEF partner and voucher registers
programmes.ident: Phase-level district lists with dates are published in the press and PEF reports - unusually easy treatment-timing data to assemble.
programmes.threats: Vouchers target urban slums, so district is a coarse treatment unit; combine with settlement-level data
programmes.evidence: Barrera-Osorio, Blakeslee, Hoover, Linden, Raju & Ryan on the rural school (NSP) experiment

programmes.name: PEF New School Program (NSP)
programmes.window: Phased across underserved districts and Cholistan; randomised in some rural rounds
programmes.stagger: Phase-in, with an embedded RCT in the 2008-2011 rural rounds
programmes.assign: Villages selected on absence of a school; the RCT randomised subsidy design
programmes.timing_src: PEF NSP registers; the associated RCT documentation
programmes.ident: Where the RCT exists, use it. Elsewhere the village-level eligibility rule (no existing school within X km) supports a geographic RD.
programmes.threats: Very local treatment - district DiD would badly dilute the effect
programmes.evidence: Barrera-Osorio et al. (2020s) on public-private partnership school entry

programmes.name: Punjab Education Sector Reform Programme (PESRP) and the school reform roadmap
programmes.agency: School Education Department, Punjab with DFID and the World Bank
programmes.window: PESRP I 2003-2009, II 2009-2015, III 2016-2020; roadmap and delivery unit from 2011
programmes.stagger: Province-wide policy with district-varying implementation intensity
programmes.assign: District league tables and stocktake schedules created differential pressure
programmes.timing_src: Punjab Monitoring & Implementation Unit records; district league tables; PMIU dashboards
programmes.ident: Not a clean on/off treatment. Best used as a continuous 'monitoring intensity' measure interacted with the roadmap start, or as a context control for other education programmes.
programmes.threats: Province-wide timing gives no untreated comparison group inside Punjab; use KP or Sindh as controls with caution
programmes.evidence: Barber (2013) practitioner account; Callen, Gulzar, Hasanain & Khan work on monitoring

programmes.name: Punjab school monitoring app / Monitoring & Evaluation Assistants (MEA) smartphone rollout
programmes.window: MEA cadre established 2011; smartphone-based data collection rolled out district by district 2012-2015
programmes.stagger: Phase-in of the digital monitoring technology
programmes.assign: Administrative rollout; some randomised variation in related experiments
programmes.timing_src: PITB and PMIU rollout records; the experimental papers
programmes.ident: Related randomised work on inspection and information disclosure gives a credible mechanism; the district rollout can extend those findings to scale.
programmes.threats: The technology and the incentive scheme changed together; measurement of absence improves mechanically when monitoring digitises
programmes.evidence: Callen, Gulzar, Hasanain, Khan & Rezaee on inspector monitoring and political economy

programmes.name: Punjab Public School Support Programme (PSSP) / PEIMA outsourced public schools
programmes.window: Phased handover of low-enrolment public schools to private operators, by district lots, 2016-2019
programmes.treated: Bahawalpur, Chiniot, Rahim Yar Khan, Muzaffargarh, Kasur and others
programmes.stagger: Phase-in by lot
programmes.assign: Schools selected on low enrolment and poor performance thresholds
programmes.timing_src: PEIMA school registers with handover dates; ITA and other operator reports
programmes.ident: School-level handover dates with an enrolment-threshold eligibility rule support both an RD and a staggered DiD, with within-district controls.
programmes.threats: Selection on low enrolment implies mean reversion; operator quality varies
programmes.evidence: Some World Bank and operator reporting; thin independent evidence

programmes.name: KP Independent Monitoring Unit and education reform
programmes.window: IMU established 2014, monitoring rolled out across districts 2014-2016
programmes.treated: All KP districts, later merged districts
programmes.stagger: Phase-in of monitoring coverage
programmes.assign: Administrative rollout
programmes.timing_src: KP IMU dashboards and monthly reports
programmes.ident: KP IMU data quality is unusually high (geo-tagged, monthly, school-level) and is one of the best administrative panels in the country.
programmes.threats: Reform bundle - monitoring, teacher recruitment reform and stipends moved together
programmes.evidence: Some governance literature; causal work limited

programmes.name: Sindh Education Reform Programme (SERP) and school consolidation
programmes.agency: School Education & Literacy Department, Sindh with the World Bank
programmes.window: SERP I 2007-2012, II 2013-2018; school consolidation and merger waves by district
programmes.stagger: Phase-in of components (stipends, SMC grants, consolidation) by district
programmes.assign: Component-specific district selection
programmes.timing_src: Sindh SELD and World Bank project documents; SEMIS
programmes.ident: Component-by-component district timing is the usable variation; the umbrella programme itself is province-wide.
programmes.threats: Multiple overlapping components make it hard to attribute effects to any single one
programmes.evidence: World Bank ICRs; limited independent evaluation

programmes.name: Punjab Daanish Schools
programmes.agency: Daanish Schools & Centres of Excellence Authority
programmes.window: Campuses opened district by district from 2010, concentrated in southern Punjab
programmes.stagger: Sequential campus openings
programmes.assign: Political selection of sites, mostly in south Punjab
programmes.timing_src: Daanish Authority records; Punjab ADP scheme approvals with dates
programmes.ident: Very small treated set and a highly selected student body - best used as a case study or with synthetic control rather than a large-N DiD.
programmes.threats: Selection into the school is competitive; spillovers to local schools are the more interesting outcome
programmes.evidence: None known

programmes.name: Higher education expansion: new public universities and sub-campuses
programmes.agency: Higher Education Commission and provincial governments
programmes.window: Continuous - new universities and sub-campuses chartered by district from 2002 to the present
programmes.treated: Dozens of districts gained a first campus
programmes.stagger: Staggered first-campus arrival, which is a genuine discrete event for a district
programmes.assign: Political allocation and provincial assembly charters
programmes.timing_src: HEC recognised institutions list with charter dates; provincial assembly acts; university first-intake records
programmes.ident: 'First university in the district' is a clean, dated, absorbing treatment. Outcomes: local tertiary enrolment, female enrolment (distance is a binding constraint for women), skilled wages, migration.
programmes.threats: Campus placement responds to local political power and existing enrolment demand; use pre-trends and instrument with political alignment if defensible
programmes.evidence: Thin - a substantial gap in the Pakistani literature

programmes.name: Punjab Skills Development Fund (PSDF) training rollout
programmes.agency: Punjab Skills Development Fund (Government of Punjab with DFID)
programmes.window: Established 2010; first scheme (Skills for Employability) launched June 2011 in four districts: Bahawalpur, Bahawalnagar, Lodhran and Muzaffargarh; later expanded across Punjab (all 36 districts by about 2016)
programmes.stagger: Clear multi-year district phase-in
programmes.assign: Southern (poorest) districts first, then province-wide
programmes.timing_src: PSDF MIS with scheme dates and district lots; PSDF annual reports
programmes.ident: PSDF ran several RCTs, so mechanism evidence exists; the district phase-in scales it up. Trainee-level MIS can be linked to LFS district aggregates.
programmes.threats: Deliberate targeting of poor districts; training supply concentrated in cities within districts
programmes.evidence: Cheema, Khwaja, Naseer & Shapiro on PSDF vouchers and stipends

programmes.name: NAVTTC Prime Minister's Hunarmand Pakistan / Kamyab Jawan skills programme
programmes.window: Phase 1 2020, subsequent phases with district-wise slot allocations
programmes.stagger: Continuous intensity (slots per capita) plus phase entry
programmes.assign: Political and administrative allocation of slots
programmes.timing_src: NAVTTC MIS and phase-wise district allocations; Kamyab Jawan portal
programmes.ident: Slots per working-age population gives a continuous treatment; combine with LFS district panels for employment outcomes.
programmes.threats: Allocation correlates with political alignment - which is itself a testable outcome
programmes.evidence: Little independent evaluation

programmes.name: Punjab Land Records Management Information System (LRMIS) / Arazi Record Centres
programmes.agency: Punjab Board of Revenue with the World Bank and PITB
programmes.window: Service centres operationalised 5 (2011), 26 (2012), 100 (2013), 133 (2014); all 143 centres across 36 districts by 2016-17
programmes.stagger: Sharp tehsil-by-tehsil operationalisation with recorded dates
programmes.assign: Sequencing by scanning and data-entry completion for each district's records
programmes.timing_src: PLRA and Board of Revenue ARC operationalisation registers; World Bank ISR sequence reports; PITB records
programmes.ident: The best-documented staggered e-government reform in Pakistan, and it operates at tehsil level - finer than district, so within-district variation identifies the effect free of district-level political confounds. Outcomes: mutation volumes, dispute filings, agricultural credit, land prices.
programmes.threats: Digitisation order correlates with pre-existing record quality; the patwari system persisted in parallel for years; the 2017 PLRA reorganisation is a second, separate event
programmes.evidence: Hussain & Ullah (2023, Land Use Policy); World Bank feature reporting; the credit and enforcement spillovers remain under-studied

programmes.name: Punjab e-Stamping
programmes.agency: Punjab Board of Revenue with PITB
programmes.window: Rolled out across districts from 2016
programmes.stagger: Phase-in over roughly a year
programmes.assign: Administrative rollout
programmes.timing_src: BOR and PITB rollout notifications; stamp duty collection series by district
programmes.ident: Direct fiscal outcome (stamp duty collected per transaction) and a strong complement to LRMIS. Under-declaration of property value is the mechanism of interest.
programmes.threats: Simultaneous changes to the DC valuation table and to federal property tax rules in 2016-2019
programmes.evidence: None known - a clear opening

programmes.name: Citizen Feedback Monitoring Programme (CFMP)
programmes.agency: Punjab Government with PITB and the Chief Minister's office
programmes.window: Jhang pilot 2008; province-wide expansion 2011-2014, service by service
programmes.stagger: Phase-in by district and by service type
programmes.assign: Pilot district chosen by the then-DCO; expansion administrative
programmes.timing_src: PITB CFMP records with district and service start dates; academic write-ups of the pilot
programmes.ident: Robocall feedback data are themselves a bribe-incidence outcome at scale. The service-by-service rollout allows within-district placebo services.
programmes.threats: Reporting propensity changes with the programme; phone ownership varies by district
programmes.evidence: Some governance case studies; causal evidence is thin

programmes.name: e-Khidmat Markaz one-window service centres
programmes.window: District centres opened sequentially 2016-2019
programmes.stagger: Sequential openings
programmes.assign: Administrative and political prioritisation
programmes.timing_src: PITB e-Khidmat records with opening dates; Punjab Open Data
programmes.ident: Opening dates are clean; outcomes include processing time, transaction volume and CFMP-measured satisfaction and bribery.
programmes.threats: Bundled with several back-end digitisations
programmes.evidence: None known

programmes.name: Police Station Record Management System (PSRMS) and police digitisation
programmes.window: District-wise rollout of computerised FIR and record systems 2012-2016
programmes.stagger: Phase-in by district and station
programmes.assign: Administrative sequencing
programmes.timing_src: PITB and Punjab Police rollout records; CRO crime statistics by district
programmes.ident: Reported crime rises mechanically when reporting cost falls - so treat 'reported crime' as a reporting outcome, and look for effects on case disposal and conviction instead.
programmes.threats: Measurement endogeneity is the central problem here
programmes.evidence: Some work on Punjab police reform; the digitisation event is under-used

programmes.name: Punjab Safe Cities (city surveillance and integrated command centres)
programmes.window: Lahore 2016; seven further cities announced January 2019: Kasur, Multan, Rawalpindi, Faisalabad, Sargodha, Bahawalpur and Gujranwala
programmes.stagger: Sequential city launches
programmes.assign: Population and political salience
programmes.timing_src: PSCA project documents and launch dates; Punjab ADP
programmes.ident: Only 7 treated units, so use synthetic control rather than standard DiD. Outcomes: reported crime by category, traffic violations, response times.
programmes.threats: Very few treated units; simultaneous traffic enforcement changes
programmes.evidence: None known

src.title: ARY News — Punjab CM inaugurates Lahore Safe City project
Punjab Police — 7 new Safe City projects are being established (2 Jan 2019)

programmes.correction: v2.0 correction: v1.0 omitted Kasur. Source: Punjab Police press release, 2 January 2019.

programmes.name: Local government restoration and elections
programmes.agency: Election Commission of Pakistan with provincial governments
programmes.window: Balochistan 2013; Punjab, Sindh and KP 2015; KP 2021-22 in two phases (December 2021 and March 2022); Punjab and Sindh 2022-2023
programmes.unit: District (election date and installation of elected local bodies)
programmes.stagger: Genuine staggering, especially the two-phase KP 2021-22 elections
programmes.assign: Provincial legislation and court-mandated timing
programmes.timing_src: ECP notifications and results with dates by district
programmes.ident: The KP two-phase 2021-22 local elections are close to an ideal natural experiment: same province, same rules, two dates a few months apart, sequencing driven by administrative rather than political criteria. Test it for balance.
programmes.threats: Local government powers were repeatedly suspended and restored; devolved functions vary
programmes.evidence: Some political science work; economics evidence is limited

programmes.name: FATA-KP merger and extension of the regular legal and administrative system
programmes.window: 25th Amendment May 2018; police (Levies conversion), courts, and provincial departments extended in phases 2018-2021; first provincial assembly elections July 2019
programmes.stagger: Phased extension of each institution
programmes.assign: Constitutional change, then phased administrative extension
programmes.timing_src: 25th Amendment; KP notifications extending each law and department with dates; ECP 2019 results
programmes.ident: One of the most interesting state-capacity natural experiments anywhere: formal courts and police replaced the FCR jirga system on datable schedules. The KP MICS 2019 covers merged districts.
programmes.threats: Almost no pre-merger household data exist for FATA; simultaneous military operations and IDP returns; population figures are contested
programmes.evidence: Very thin - a major open area, and a natural fit for a ReCIPE-style research agenda

programmes.name: Creation of new districts (district bifurcation)
programmes.window: Nankana Sahib 2005; Chiniot 2009; Sindh and Balochistan splits through the 2000s-2010s; Punjab created Kot Addu, Talagang, Murree, Wazirabad in 2022 and Taunsa in 2023
programmes.stagger: Staggered creation events
programmes.assign: Political decisions, often by the party in provincial power
programmes.timing_src: Provincial gazette notifications with dates; PBS district code changes
programmes.ident: 'Getting your own district' means a new DC, DHQ hospital, district education office and budget line - a discrete jump in local administrative presence. Outcomes: service delivery, public employment, nightlights in the new headquarters town.
programmes.threats: Splits are politically chosen; the panel must be re-based to constant boundaries (harmonise to pre-split parents) before any analysis
programmes.evidence: Almost nothing in the Pakistani literature; a strong, feasible paper

programmes.name: Right to Information legislation
programmes.window: KP and Punjab 2013; Sindh 2016; Balochistan 2021; federal 2017
programmes.stagger: Province-level staggering only
programmes.assign: Legislative politics
programmes.timing_src: Provincial acts with commencement dates; information commission annual reports
programmes.tq_note: High for dates, but the unit is coarse
programmes.ident: Four treated units at province level is too few for a district DiD, but the RTI request data themselves (requests filed per district) give a district-level compliance outcome.
programmes.threats: Only four units; enforcement varies enormously from the statute
programmes.evidence: Some governance literature

programmes.name: 3G/4G spectrum award and mobile broadband coverage expansion
programmes.window: Spectrum auctioned April 2014; operator coverage expanded district by district 2014-2020; 4G reached ~95% of networks by 2025
programmes.stagger: Continuous coverage expansion with district-specific arrival dates
programmes.assign: Commercial - operators covered dense and high-ARPU districts first
programmes.timing_src: GSMA/Collins Bartholomew Mobile Coverage Explorer annual polygons; OpenCellID; PTA annual reports; Ookla from 2019
programmes.ident: Coverage arrival dates give a strong staggered design, but rollout is commercially endogenous. Instrument with terrain ruggedness, distance to fibre backbone, or use the USF-subsidised lots (P46) as the exogenous component.
programmes.threats: Endogenous commercial placement is the central threat; smartphone affordability moved simultaneously
programmes.evidence: Some work on mobile money in Pakistan; district broadband effects are largely unstudied

programmes.name: Universal Service Fund subsidised broadband and optical fibre projects
programmes.agency: Universal Service Fund Company, Ministry of IT
programmes.window: Continuous - project lots tendered, awarded and completed by district/tehsil from 2007 to the present
programmes.unit: Project lot (tehsil / district) with award and completion dates
programmes.stagger: Staggered lot completion
programmes.assign: Lots defined by 'unserved and underserved' criteria and awarded by reverse auction to the lowest subsidy bid
programmes.timing_src: USF project pages listing lots, districts, award dates, completion dates and subsidy amounts
programmes.ident: This is the exogenous complement to P45: the subsidy rule targets commercially unattractive areas, and the auction determines timing. Excellent instrument or standalone treatment.
programmes.threats: Completion dates lag award dates and reported completion is not always real coverage
programmes.evidence: Very little - one of the most under-used public datasets in Pakistan

programmes.name: Motorway and expressway network expansion (incl. CPEC corridors)
programmes.agency: National Highway Authority; provincial highway departments
programmes.window: M-1 2007, M-4 sections 2015-2019, M-5 Multan-Sukkur 2019, M-11 Lahore-Sialkot 2020, M-14 Hakla-DI Khan 2021
programmes.unit: Road section, mapped to districts crossed and interchange locations
programmes.stagger: Staggered section openings with recorded dates
programmes.assign: Route selection is political and topographic
programmes.timing_src: NHA project completion records; CPEC portal; OSM historical extracts
programmes.ident: Use distance to the nearest interchange rather than 'district crossed' - the treatment is access, not adjacency. A least-cost-path counterfactual route is the standard instrument.
programmes.threats: Routes are chosen to connect places already growing; the classic endogenous-placement problem
programmes.evidence: Some CPEC descriptive work; rigorous Pakistani road-effect papers are scarce

programmes.name: Khadim-e-Punjab Rural Roads Programme
programmes.window: Package-wise rural road construction across districts 2015-2018
programmes.stagger: Staggered package completion
programmes.assign: District allocations announced with political inputs
programmes.timing_src: Punjab C&W and P&D scheme registers with completion dates; ADP releases
programmes.ident: Package-level completion dates plus mouza-level road access from the Mouza Census 2008 and 2020 allow a fairly tight design.
programmes.threats: Political allocation of packages; the Mouza Census gap (2008 to 2020) is long
programmes.evidence: None known

programmes.name: Rural electrification and grid station expansion
programmes.window: New grid stations and feeder expansions notified by district throughout the 2000s-2010s
programmes.stagger: Continuous, with datable grid-station commissioning
programmes.assign: Load growth and political priority
programmes.timing_src: DISCO annual reports; NEPRA state of industry reports; nightlights as a proxy
programmes.ident: Administrative dates are hard to obtain; nightlights and PSLM connection rates are the practical route.
programmes.threats: Load-shedding hours (quality) matter more than connection status in Pakistan, and are poorly measured
programmes.evidence: Some work on load-shedding and firms

programmes.name: Sui gas network expansion
programmes.window: Town and district connections notified over time; new connections were suspended nationally in 2021
programmes.stagger: Staggered arrival of piped gas
programmes.assign: Proximity to transmission network plus political allocation of schemes
programmes.timing_src: SNGPL/SSGC scheme registers; OGRA annual reports; PSLM cooking-fuel module
programmes.ident: PSLM's cooking-fuel question gives a household-level verification of network arrival. Outcomes: fuel switching, indoor air pollution, female time use, firm energy costs.
programmes.threats: Scheme allocation is famously political (a testable outcome in itself)
programmes.evidence: Very thin

programmes.name: Punjab Irrigated-Agriculture Productivity Improvement Project (drip/sprinkler and watercourse lining)
programmes.agency: Agriculture Department, Punjab with the World Bank
programmes.window: District-wise subsidy allocations and watercourse improvement schemes 2012-2020
programmes.stagger: Continuous intensity plus scheme completion dates
programmes.assign: Applications from farmers, subject to district quotas
programmes.timing_src: PIPIP MIS with scheme locations and completion dates; On-Farm Water Management directorate records
programmes.ident: Scheme-level GPS with completion dates supports a within-district design; NDVI and Crop Reporting Service yields give outcomes at matching resolution.
programmes.threats: Farmer self-selection into subsidies; quota allocation across districts is administrative
programmes.evidence: World Bank ICR; limited independent work

programmes.name: Branchless banking and mobile money agent network expansion
programmes.agency: Telenor/Easypaisa, Jazz/JazzCash, others under SBP regulation
programmes.window: Easypaisa launched 2009; agent networks expanded district by district through the 2010s
programmes.stagger: Continuous intensity
programmes.assign: Commercial placement, correlated with population and mobile coverage
programmes.timing_src: SBP Branchless Banking Newsletter (quarterly); operator disclosures; PSLM account ownership
programmes.ident: Best combined with P45/P46: broadband coverage is a plausible instrument for agent entry. Interacts directly with BISP payment digitisation (P03).
programmes.threats: Commercial endogeneity; agent counts are reported at coarse geography
programmes.evidence: Some work on Easypaisa; district-level analysis is limited

programmes.name: Microfinance branch and portfolio expansion
programmes.agency: Microfinance banks and institutions under SBP/PMN
programmes.window: Continuous district-by-district branch expansion, documented quarterly since 2007
programmes.stagger: Continuous intensity with datable branch openings
programmes.assign: Commercial and social-mission placement
programmes.timing_src: PMN MicroWatch quarterly district penetration tables (a genuinely excellent public dataset)
programmes.ident: MicroWatch gives quarterly district-level penetration back to 2007 - one of the few high-frequency district panels available for free. Use branch openings as events.
programmes.threats: Placement follows demand; competition among MFIs changes measured penetration
programmes.evidence: Some microfinance impact work; district panel analysis is under-used

programmes.name: SBP Credit Guarantee Scheme and agricultural credit targets
programmes.agency: State Bank of Pakistan with commercial banks
programmes.window: Scheme launched 2010; district-wise indicative credit targets set annually
programmes.stagger: Continuous intensity
programmes.assign: SBP allocation formula based on cultivated area and past disbursement
programmes.timing_src: SBP agricultural credit disbursement by district and bank (annual); SBP circulars
programmes.ident: Direct interaction with land digitisation (P35): titles become usable collateral. This is the natural spillover test for the LRMIS agenda.
programmes.threats: Targets are indicative, not binding; disbursement is reported by branch location, not borrower location
programmes.evidence: Thin - a clear opening at the credit-land intersection

programmes.name: Punjab Kisan Card / e-Credit Scheme
programmes.agency: Agriculture Department, Punjab with Bank of Punjab
programmes.window: District-wise enrolment of farmers from 2018-19; relaunched 2024-25
programmes.stagger: Phase-in
programmes.assign: Land records verification through LRMIS - so eligibility is mechanically linked to digitisation
programmes.timing_src: Punjab Agriculture Department and Bank of Punjab MIS; LRMIS linkage records
programmes.ident: The eligibility rule (a verified digital land record) makes LRMIS completion a first stage for Kisan Card access. That is an unusually clean two-step design.
programmes.threats: Only landowners are eligible, so tenants are mechanically excluded - a distributional outcome in itself
programmes.evidence: None known

programmes.name: Prime Minister's Kamyab Jawan Youth Entrepreneurship Scheme
programmes.window: District-wise loan disbursement from 2019
programmes.stagger: Continuous intensity
programmes.assign: Bank-level credit decisions; regional quotas
programmes.timing_src: SBP and Kamyab Jawan MIS; bank disclosures
programmes.ident: Disbursement per capita gives a continuous treatment, but selection into borrowing is severe.
programmes.threats: Loan approval is endogenous to applicant quality
programmes.evidence: None known

programmes.name: Punjab Model Bazaars / Sahulat Bazaars
programmes.window: Bazaars opened district by district from 2011
programmes.stagger: Sequential openings
programmes.assign: Political and urban prioritisation
programmes.timing_src: PMBMC bazaar registers with opening dates; Punjab ADP
programmes.ident: Directly testable on retail price outcomes using PBS city price data and AMIS mandi prices around opening dates.
programmes.threats: Bazaars are urban and few; price effects may be local to a neighbourhood
programmes.evidence: None known

programmes.name: Major military operations (Rah-e-Rast, Rah-e-Nijat, Zarb-e-Azb, Radd-ul-Fasaad, Khyber series)
programmes.window: Swat (Rah-e-Rast) 2009; South Waziristan (Rah-e-Nijat) 2009-10; North Waziristan (Zarb-e-Azb) June 2014; Radd-ul-Fasaad from February 2017
programmes.unit: Agency / district (operation start and clearance date)
programmes.stagger: Staggered by operation with well-documented start dates
programmes.assign: Militant presence - explicitly endogenous to the outcome
programmes.timing_src: ISPR announcements; BFRS and GTD event data; IDP registration records
programmes.tq_note: High for dates, but assignment is deeply endogenous
programmes.ident: The identification problem is severe: operations occur precisely where violence is highest. Realistic designs use spillovers to neighbouring untreated districts, or the timing of IDP return (which is administratively scheduled) rather than the operation itself.
programmes.threats: Reverse causality is the defining problem; displacement means the population itself changes
programmes.evidence: Fair, Hamza, Shapiro and co-authors on Pakistani conflict; Hussain & Yoon (2025, Labour Economics) uses the bin Laden death as an alternative shock

src.title: ISPR announcements, compiled in BFRS / GTD event data
ISPR announcements, compiled in BFRS / GTD event data

programmes.name: US drone strike campaign
programmes.window: Strikes concentrated 2008-2014, declining to 2018
programmes.stagger: Continuous strike intensity with precise dates
programmes.assign: Targeting is endogenous to militant presence
programmes.timing_src: New America Foundation, Bureau of Investigative Journalism, Long War Journal strike databases
programmes.tq_note: High for strike dates and locations
programmes.ident: Precise dates and locations, but no household data for the affected areas and severe endogeneity. Best used with high-frequency outcomes (violence, migration into settled districts) rather than welfare outcomes.
programmes.threats: No survey coverage of FATA pre-merger; targeting endogeneity
programmes.evidence: Fair et al. on drone strikes and public opinion; Johnston & Sarbahi (2016)

programmes.name: National Action Plan and post-APS security surge
programmes.window: Announced December 2014-January 2015; components (military courts, madrassa registration, Fourth Schedule enforcement) implemented at different times by province and district
programmes.stagger: Component-by-component and province-by-province variation
programmes.assign: Political and security prioritisation
programmes.timing_src: NACTA reports; provincial home department notifications; PIPS annual reports
programmes.ident: Poorly documented at district level. Realistically usable only as a national break point unless component-level district records can be obtained.
programmes.threats: Simultaneous with Zarb-e-Azb; national timing gives no control group
programmes.evidence: Descriptive PIPS reporting

programmes.name: IDP registration and phased return to merged districts
programmes.agency: FATA/KP Disaster Management Authority with UNHCR
programmes.window: Phased return schedules by agency and tehsil, 2015-2018
programmes.stagger: Administratively scheduled staggered returns
programmes.assign: Security clearance and reconstruction readiness - administrative and datable
programmes.timing_src: FDMA return notifications; UNHCR and IOM return monitoring; HDX
programmes.ident: Return dates are administratively set rather than chosen by households, which is a much better source of variation than the operations themselves. Combine with KP MICS 2019.
programmes.threats: Returnees are selected; destination infrastructure was rebuilt simultaneously
programmes.evidence: Very thin

programmes.name: 2010 super-flood and the Watan Card emergency transfer
programmes.window: Flooding July-September 2010; Watan Card payments from late 2010 through 2011
programmes.stagger: Continuous treatment intensity plus a discrete calamity notification
programmes.assign: Hydrology - flood extent is plausibly exogenous conditional on river distance and elevation
programmes.timing_src: UNOSAT and Dartmouth Flood Observatory inundation rasters; PDMA calamity notifications; NADRA Watan Card records
programmes.ident: Inundation share from satellite gives a continuous, credibly exogenous treatment intensity. The Watan Card transfer is a second, nested treatment among the flood-affected.
programmes.threats: Flood exposure correlates with river proximity and land quality; the 2010-11 PSLM wave straddles the event (both a problem and an opportunity)
programmes.evidence: Gioli et al.; Kurosaki; several papers exist but the district panel is not exhausted

programmes.name: 2022 floods and post-flood response
programmes.window: June-October 2022; BISP flood relief payments late 2022
programmes.stagger: Continuous intensity
programmes.assign: Hydrology
programmes.timing_src: Sentinel-1 SAR flood maps; PDNA 2022; PDMA reports; BISP payment records
programmes.ident: PSLM 2019-20 gives a genuine district-representative baseline immediately before the shock - unusually good timing for a DiD.
programmes.threats: Post-flood survey coverage is limited so far; overlaps with the 2022-23 macroeconomic crisis
programmes.evidence: World Bank PDNA; emerging literature

programmes.name: 2005 Kashmir earthquake and reconstruction (ERRA)
programmes.window: 8 October 2005; reconstruction grants disbursed in tranches 2006-2010
programmes.unit: District / union council (damage intensity and grant tranche)
programmes.stagger: Continuous damage intensity plus staggered grant tranches
programmes.assign: Seismic exposure - distance to fault rupture is exogenous
programmes.timing_src: ERRA housing reconstruction records; USGS ShakeMap; damage assessments
programmes.ident: Distance to the fault line is the standard exogenous intensity measure. ERRA's tranche schedule adds staggered financial treatment.
programmes.threats: Very small affected area; massive concurrent aid inflow
programmes.evidence: Andrabi & Das (2017, ReStat) on aid and learning; Andrabi, Daniels & Das (2023) on human capital

src.title: Earthquake Reconstruction & Rehabilitation Authority — affected districts

programmes.name: Locust invasion and calamity declarations
programmes.window: Swarms 2019-2020; district calamity notifications issued at different dates
programmes.stagger: Staggered notification with swarm arrival dates
programmes.assign: Entomology and wind patterns - plausibly exogenous
programmes.timing_src: FAO Locust Watch swarm records with coordinates and dates; NDMA notifications; Crop Reporting Service yields
programmes.ident: FAO's swarm database gives dated, geocoded arrivals - a genuinely exogenous agricultural shock with district-level timing.
programmes.threats: Overlaps with COVID-19 in 2020; reporting of swarms may be incomplete
programmes.evidence: Very thin - a feasible and original paper

programmes.name: Osama bin Laden killing (national salience shock with differential district exposure)
programmes.unit: National event; district exposure varies with pre-period conflict intensity
programmes.stagger: Single date, heterogeneous exposure
programmes.assign: Exogenous timing; exposure proxied by baseline terrorism intensity
programmes.timing_src: GTD/BFRS baseline intensity; PSLM 2010-11 and 2012-13
programmes.ident: Uses a sharp national date interacted with continuous district exposure - avoids the endogenous-placement problem entirely.
programmes.threats: Exposure intensity is itself correlated with district characteristics; requires strong pre-trend evidence
programmes.evidence: Hussain & Yoon (2025, Labour Economics) - terrorism and education

programmes.name: 2017 census, delimitation and constituency redistricting
programmes.window: Census 2017; delimitation 2018; second delimitation after the 2023 census
programmes.stagger: Discrete reallocation events
programmes.assign: Population-rule-based reallocation of seats
programmes.timing_src: ECP delimitation reports; census district populations
programmes.ident: Seat reallocation follows a population formula, so districts just above or below a seat threshold form a natural discontinuity in political representation.
programmes.threats: Census figures were themselves politically contested; boundaries changed twice in six years
programmes.evidence: Some political science work

datasets.notes: Workhorse for district panels. CAUTION: the 2010-11 wave is easy to drop silently; district codes change with new district creation.

datasets.dataset: Household Integrated Economic Survey (consumption module)
datasets.district_id: Province-rep; district only in PSLM-linked rounds

datasets.dataset: Labour Force Survey

datasets.notes: Best source for employment status, sector, hours, wages, informality.

datasets.dataset: National Nutrition Survey
datasets.producer: Ministry of NHSR&C / Aga Khan University / UNICEF

datasets.dataset: Punjab Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey (MICS)

datasets.dataset: Sindh MICS

datasets.dataset: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa MICS

datasets.dataset: Pakistan Demographic and Health Survey
